title: Server Actions vs Route Handlers
description: Choose an interface for the caller you actually have.

questions.question: Does using a Server Action remove the need for authorization?
questions.answer: No. Treat the action as a callable mutation boundary. Authenticate and authorize the specific operation on the server.

questions.question: When does a Route Handler fit better?
questions.answer: When a webhook, external client, or other caller needs an explicit HTTP API rather than React’s action integration.

facts: Validate request bodies at runtime.
Return safe, consistent errors.
Shared mutation rules belong below the transport interface.
quizDistractors: Yes. A hidden Action can never be called without the matching button.

children.value: A Server Action is a server function integrated with React-driven mutations. A Route Handler implements an HTTP endpoint with an explicit method, request, and response. Both cross a trust boundary and require input validation and access checks.

Use an Action for an app form when that integration fits. Use a Route Handler for webhooks, external clients, or an HTTP contract you intend to expose. Do not duplicate the business rules in both; keep validation and mutation logic in a shared server layer.
Do not assume a hidden button protects a server function. The permission check must run at the actual data or mutation boundary.

title: Streaming AI output: stop, retry & failures
description: Treat partial output as an unfinished result.

questions.question: Does a network chunk always equal one complete model message?
questions.answer: No. Transport chunk boundaries are independent of application framing. Decode text safely and parse the endpoint’s actual protocol.

questions.question: Should Stop be displayed as a server failure?
questions.answer: No. Represent intentional cancellation distinctly, preserve useful partial output when appropriate, and make a new attempt an explicit action.

questions.question: Why guard chunks with a request version?
questions.answer: Cancellation may arrive after a callback is queued; version checks prevent obsolete requests from updating the current UI.

questions.question: Does a retry continue the same model response?
questions.answer: Not automatically. Treat it as a new attempt unless the server protocol explicitly supports safe resumption.

facts: A 200 status does not guarantee that a stream finishes.
Do not expose provider secrets in browser code.
Test disconnects and malformed protocol events.

title: API validation, status codes & pagination contracts
description: Define successful responses and failures before writing the UI.

questions.question: Does fetch reject on a 404 response?
questions.answer: No. Check response.ok or status; fetch normally rejects for transport failures or aborts, not HTTP error statuses.

questions.question: Why use a tie-breaker in cursor pagination?
questions.answer: Equal timestamps otherwise make ordering ambiguous; a unique ID provides a stable total order.

questions.question: Can TypeScript replace server validation?
questions.answer: No. Types disappear at runtime, and clients can send arbitrary bytes.

questions.question: When is a retry dangerous?
questions.answer: When a mutation may already have committed but its response was lost; retry using a server-enforced idempotency contract or first reconcile the result.

facts: No. Check response.ok or status; fetch normally rejects for transport failures or aborts, not HTTP error statuses.
Equal timestamps otherwise make ordering ambiguous; a unique ID provides a stable total order.
No. Types disappear at runtime, and clients can send arbitrary bytes.
quizDistractors: This can be assumed without checking inputs, ownership, or failures.
The UI alone guarantees correctness for all callers.

children.value: Define successful responses and failures before writing the UI.

GET reads and must not perform a requested mutation. PUT describes replacement and is idempotent by intended effect. PATCH describes a partial change and is not inherently idempotent. DELETE is idempotent by intended effect even if later responses differ. POST is not inherently idempotent; use an agreed idempotency key when retries could duplicate a purchase or job.

Use 200 for a successful body, 201 for creation (often with Location), 202 for accepted work that is not finished, and 204 for success without a body. A 304 is cache validation, not a JSON success body. Distinguish malformed input (400), missing/invalid authentication (401), insufficient permission (403), absence (404), conflicting current state (409), failed preconditions (412), semantically invalid content (422 under your API convention), throttling (429), and server failure (5xx). Avoid leaking stack traces, SQL or private resource existence.

Treat JSON as unknown. Check object shape, required fields, lengths, allowed enum values and cross-field rules. Reject or deliberately strip unknown keys; never pass unfiltered input into a database update. Client validation improves feedback; server validation enforces the contract. Limit body size and list size. Return stable error codes, safe messages and field paths; retain a request ID in server logs.

Offset pagination is simple but inserts can shift pages. Cursor pagination uses a stable total order, for example created_at plus unique id. Encode and validate both cursor values; scope the query to the authenticated owner on every page. Fetch limit + 1 to determine hasNextPage. Cursors are positions, not permission tokens. title: Authentication, authorization, sessions & OAuth
description: Prove identity separately from granting permission.

questions.question: Does authentication automatically authorize every record?
questions.answer: No. After identifying a user, check their permission for the requested operation and resource.

questions.question: Is the payload of a signed JWT necessarily secret?
questions.answer: No. Signing protects integrity, not confidentiality. Do not put secrets into an ordinary signed token payload.

facts: Use secure cookie attributes appropriate to the deployment.

children.value: Authentication establishes who is making a request. Authorization decides whether that identity may perform a particular action on a particular resource. A session cookie or token is a mechanism for carrying identity-related state; neither is permission by itself.

title: Binary search with a half-open interval
description: Keep the candidate range and exit condition consistent.

questions.question: Does lower bound always return an exact target match?
questions.answer: No. It returns the first position whose value is at least the target, or the array length. Check the value if an exact match is required.

questions.answer: Without strict progress, the loop may revisit the same bounds indefinitely. Align updates with the interval convention.

Yes. It returns -1 whenever there is no exact match.

children.value: Binary search repeatedly discards a portion of an ordered search space. A lower-bound search finds the first index whose value is at least the target. Using a half-open interval [left, right) makes the empty-range condition left === right straightforward.

Write the invariant before the loop: values before left are too small, and right is an excluded boundary. Lower bound is not automatically an exact match, so check the returned index and value if the caller asks whether a target exists.

title: Browser rendering & layout work
description: Know what happens between receiving HTML and painting pixels.

questions.question: Why can a geometry read be expensive?
questions.answer: If pending style changes invalidate layout, a geometry read may force the browser to calculate it synchronously before returning the value.

questions.question: Is transform always free?
questions.answer: No. It often avoids layout, but compositing, rasterization, large layers, and other work still have costs. Profile the actual interaction.

facts: A fast network response does not guarantee a responsive UI.

title: Closures, without the confusion
description: Understand how functions remember the scope they were created in.

questions.question: Does a closure copy a variable?
questions.answer: No. It retains access to the lexical binding. Later changes to that binding can be observed by the closure.

questions.question: Why does let help inside a loop?
questions.answer: A let declaration in a for loop creates a new binding for each iteration. Callbacks can therefore retain different iteration values.

questions.question: Can closures retain memory?
questions.answer: Yes. Values reachable through a retained closure remain reachable. Remove listeners and subscriptions when they are no longer needed.

Each call to the outer function can create an independent lexical environment.
A retained closure can keep referenced objects in memory.

title: Debounce & throttle
description: Choose between waiting for quiet and limiting frequency.

questions.question: Does debouncing guarantee that an older request cannot win?
questions.answer: No. It reduces how often requests start. Once multiple requests exist, cancellation or a request-identity check is still needed.

questions.question: Why clean up the debounce timer?
questions.answer: A pending callback may run after its owner is gone. Canceling it prevents unnecessary work and callbacks against stale state.

questions.question: Does this throttle deliver the final event automatically?
questions.answer: No. It is leading-only; trailing delivery requires a separate timer and explicit semantics.

facts: Debounce and throttle solve different timing problems.
A debounce interval is a product decision, not a universal constant.
Do not delay local filtering just because network search needs debouncing.
quizDistractors: Yes. A debounce cancels every previously started network request.
Yes. Debounce makes responses arrive in request order.

children.value: Debouncing delays work until calls have stopped for an interval. Throttling limits how often work runs during a continuous stream. A search request often benefits from trailing debounce; a scroll-driven update may need throttling or requestAnimationFrame depending on its purpose.

A 300 ms debounce reduces request frequency, but it does not resolve out-of-order responses. Request cancellation and stale-result protection solve that separate problem. Clear pending timers when the owning component or subscription is disposed.
Recreating the debounced function on every render gives each instance its own timer. Keep ownership stable or implement the timer within an Effect.

description: Find the receiver by looking at how a function is called.

questions.question: Does an ordinary function keep this from where it was defined?
questions.answer: No. Its receiver usually comes from how it is called. Arrow functions instead capture lexical this.

questions.question: Why does an arrow ignore call(otherObject)?

A regular function receives this according to how it is called. A detached strict-mode call has undefined this; reading this.name then throws. bind creates a function with a fixed receiver; call invokes with individual arguments, apply with an argument list. title: Trees: breadth-first & depth-first traversal
description: Choose a queue or stack according to the exploration order.

questions.question: Which traversal naturally visits a tree level by level?
questions.answer: Breadth-first search, using a queue. Nodes discovered earlier at the current frontier are processed before their deeper descendants.

questions.question: Why might an iterative DFS be preferable to recursive DFS?
questions.answer: It avoids depending on the language runtime’s recursion depth limit for a very deep tree.

questions.question: When does BFS use more memory than DFS?
questions.answer: A very wide tree can require a large BFS frontier while DFS keeps a path and deferred branches.

facts: A general graph may require visited-state tracking.
Traversal order and output order are contract choices.

quizDistractors: Depth-first search always visits every shallower node first.
A recursive call automatically gives breadth-first ordering.

children.value: Breadth-first traversal explores by distance in edges from the root; depth-first traversal follows one branch before returning to alternatives. A queue expresses BFS. A stack or recursion expresses DFS. Trees do not need a visited set when the structure truly has no cycles and each child is reached once.

The traversal touches each node once in O(n) time. Extra space depends on maximum width for BFS or depth/pending branches for DFS. Use an explicit stack when recursion depth can exceed the runtime’s call-stack limit.

questions.question: Why does moving the left pointer help when the sorted pair sum is too small?

questions.question: Why check the complement before inserting the current index?

unknown forces a check before use; any disables that protection. A type assertion does not validate bytes. Narrow unions using a discriminant and make exhaustive switches fail on unhandled variants. title: XSS, CSRF, CORS, injection & secrets
description: Match each threat to the boundary it crosses.

questions.question: Does CORS replace server authorization?
questions.answer: No. CORS governs certain browser cross-origin access. Non-browser callers still need authentication, authorization, and input validation.

questions.question: Why use parameterized SQL?
questions.answer: Parameters are treated as data rather than executable query syntax, preventing the input from rewriting the query structure.
